I didn't want to use that cause in principle it could be an overflow unless we enforce the minimum gas limit gas_limit // 1024 could be zero at genesis for example seems like the "spec" has the same issue ```python def expected_gas_limit(parent_gas_limit, target_gas_limit): max_gas_limit_difference = (parent_gas_limit // 1024) - 1 if target_gas_limit > parent_gas_limit: gas_diff = target_gas_limit - parent_gas_limit return parent_gas_limit + min(gas_diff, max_gas_limit_difference) else: gas_diff = parent_gas_limit - target_gas_limit return parent_gas_limit - min(gas_diff, max_gas_limit_difference) ``` but I don't remember from where I got this python snippet The spec enforces a parent gas limit of at least 5000 isn't it? I am not even sure what is "the spec", I am just collecting breadcrumps across EIPs Lol, yeah in EIP 1559, the limit of 5000 is enforced ```python # check if the block changed the gas limit too much assert block.gas_limit < parent_gas_limit + parent_gas_limit // 1024, assert block.gas_limit > parent_gas_limit - parent_gas_limit // 1024, # check if the gas limit is at least the minimum gas limit assert block.gas_limit >= 5000 ``` https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-1559.md#specification By the way my solution also has this overflow in the Max So anyway it's cooked 🙂 it would take ~3.8 million years for that to happen if we started to bump the gas limit now to `2^64 - 1` 🙂 No no the max overflows if the parent gas limit is zero Which on the CL can happen at genesis ah you mean that ok, we can just do `max(..., 0)`? Is that the actual minimum? that's how it's defined in EIP-1559 I would assume all ELs implement it that way Oh. Well in that case, yes. It will make testing easier. it cant be less than 1024, otherwise it stuck at whatever parent gas limit value we have ```python @with_gloas_and_later @spec_test @single_phase def test_parent_gas_limit_underflows(spec): # parent_gas_limit // 1024 = 0; max(0, 1) - 1 = 0 (guard prevents underflow) assert spec.is_gas_limit_target_compatible(1023, 1023, 60_000_000) ``` passes in the current code, but feels wrong to even have this scenario tested found the actual execution specs function https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/forks/amsterdam/src/ethereum/forks/london/fork.py#L873-L910 has the same 5000 as min <@586161934425128960> How do you feel about defining constants for `GAS_COSTS_LIMIT_ADJUSTMENT_FACTOR` and `GAS_COSTS_LIMIT_MINIMUM` in the CL? I didn't want to add 5000 in my PR cause I wanted to explicitly deal with genesis differently I do not want to force the genesis bid to have a non-trivial minimum it seems arbitrary what value should the genesis bid have? I think anything, could be zero for all I know I don't want to keep a spec constant that has to be in pair with the EL if it's less than 1024 based on the transition rule it cannot increase the proposer can include any bid it's not a consensus issue they won't propagate so slot 1 fixes this so you just mean the CL side, and EL genesis block would have a different gas limit? yes I want to avoid sync issues because first EL block has to pass https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/forks/amsterdam/src/ethereum/forks/london/fork.py#L907-L908 that are unnessary burden these checks we are adding here are on a p2p topic for public bids, they are not a matter of consensus so the current spec matches at least with how lodestar, prysm, and teku have it implemented today I pushed some basic tests, we can later convert to gossip validation tests I removed this test, so the underflow case is not tested I'm fine with whatever, the current code matches well with what we have in lodestar though 🙂 I was obviously joking, overloading the conversion of boolean to int in Python is crazy it's fine with the max, I rather have the max than another constant it looks fancy though
